memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "And for your lifeblood I will surely demand an accounting. I will demand an accounting from every animal. And from each human being, too, I will demand an accounting for the life of another human being." - Gen 9:5 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God speaks with great seriousness here: "for your lifeblood I will surely demand an accounting." Human life is so precious to God that He personally holds accountable anyone who takes it. Nothing is overlooked; no injustice escapes His notice. The God who made every person will require a reckoning for every life wrongfully destroyed.

This is a solemn but comforting truth. We live in a world where violence often seems to go unpunished, where the powerful crush the weak and appear to get away with it. But God says otherwise. He sees, He remembers, and He will one day call every person to account. Justice may be delayed, but with God it is never denied.

For victims of injustice, this brings deep comfort. Your suffering is not invisible to God. He is not indifferent to the wrongs done to you. He will "demand an accounting," and He will set all things right in His time.

For all of us, it is a sobering call to reverence for life and to leave vengeance in God's hands. "It is mine to avenge; I will repay, says the Lord" (Rom 12:19). We do not need to take justice into our own hands, because God is the perfect Judge. And wonderfully, at the cross, God's justice and mercy meet - Jesus bore the accounting we deserved, so that guilty sinners could be forgiven. The God who demands an accounting is also the God who provided the payment Himself.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you believe God sees and will account for every injustice?
- Can you leave vengeance in God's hands, trusting Him as the perfect Judge?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Righteous God, thank You that no injustice escapes You and You will set all things right. Help me trust You as the perfect Judge and leave vengeance in Your hands. Thank You that at the cross, mercy met justice for me.
